title: Power Automate: Delinea Secret Server as a credential provider for desktop flows
summary: The roadmap facts and existing credential controls are supported, and searches confirmed the provider-specific documentation gaps. The description of a stored identity retrieving a privileged password goes beyond the evidence. The logging assurance should also acknowledge Microsoft's sensitive-variable security advisory.

claims.claim: No Microsoft Learn page describing the Delinea provider was found at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: "Delinea" "Power Automate"; "Delinea" "credential" Power Automate licensing default setup API authentication troubleshooting. Opened both cited credential guides and the credential reference; search results documented other providers, not Delinea.

claims.claim: The Delinea provider's default state is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate Delinea Secret Server credential provider setup authentication permissions licensing meter default availability. Read the roadmap and both cited credential guides; none states a Delinea default or admin-enablement requirement.

claims.claim: CyberArk credentials retrieve CCP CyberArk secrets from the vault at runtime.
claims.quote: This feature enables you to create a Power Automate credential that retrieves CCP CyberArk secrets from the vault during runtime.

claims.claim: An Azure Key Vault credential used in a desktop flow connection signs into the machine at runtime for attended and unattended runs.
claims.quote: Used in a desktop flow connection, the credential is used to sign into the machine during runtime (attended and unattended runs).

claims.claim: For CyberArk, the Get credential variable is sensitive and its value is not stored in logs.
claims.quote: This variable is marked as sensitive and can't be modified. This restriction means the value of this variable isn't stored in the logs.
claims.fix: Keep the documented behaviour but cite https://learn.microsoft.com/troubleshoot/power-platform/power-automate/desktop-flows/sensitive-variables-security-update: affected 2.62-2.66 builds can expose global sensitive variables used in local subflows; patched builds or 2.67.143.26090 and later fix it.

claims.claim: For Azure Key Vault, the Get credential variable is sensitive and its value is not stored in logs.
claims.quote: This variable is marked as "sensitive" and can't be changed. This means the value of this variable isn't stored in the logs.
claims.fix: Qualify the shared logging assurance with https://learn.microsoft.com/troubleshoot/power-platform/power-automate/desktop-flows/sensitive-variables-security-update: affected 2.62-2.66 builds can log global sensitive values used in local subflows; install a listed patched build or 2.67.143.26090 or later.

claims.claim: The CyberArk certificate is opened and encrypted with the machine group's public key so only registered machines can read it.
claims.quote: The certificate is opened and encrypted by using the public key of the machine group so it's only readable from the registered machines.

claims.claim: A CyberArk application cannot currently be associated with machines or groups shared with other users.
claims.quote: You can't currently associate a CyberArk application with machines or groups that you share with other users.

claims.claim: CyberArk credential use at runtime requires a registered machine, including local attended or debugging runs.
claims.quote: The registered machine is required for credentials to work properly at runtime, even for local attended or debugging runs.

claims.claim: Azure Key Vault credential use at runtime requires a registered machine, including local attended or debugging runs.
claims.quote: The registered machine is required for credentials to work properly at runtime, even for local attended or debugging runs.

claims.claim: The documented CyberArk credential feature is currently unavailable for US Government Clouds.
claims.quote: Currently, this feature isn't available for US Government Clouds.

claims.claim: The documented Azure Key Vault credential feature is currently unavailable for US Government Clouds.
claims.quote: Currently, this feature isn't available for US Government Clouds.

claims.claim: Sharing an Azure Key Vault credential also shares all its environment variables.
claims.quote: By sharing your credential, all the environment variables used in the credential are shared as well.

claims.claim: Removing permissions on an Azure Key Vault credential does not remove permissions on its environment variables.
claims.quote: Removing permissions on a credential doesn't remove permissions on the environment variables.

claims.claim: CyberArk application and certificate configuration is available in Power Automate under Machines > machine or group > Configure CyberArk.
claims.quote: From the left navigation, select Machines, and then select the machine or the group. In the Machine details, select Configure CyberArk.

claims.claim: An API for configuring a CyberArk application on Power Automate machines or groups is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate CyberArk machine application configure API PowerShell. Opened Create a CyberArk credential and credential EntityType; results document portal configuration, secret-retrieval actions and machine registration, not an equivalent configuration API.

claims.claim: Credential sharing is available in Power Automate under Credentials > credential > Share.
claims.quote: Sign-in to Power Automate, and then go to Credentials. Select your credential from the list of credentials. On the command bar, select Share.

claims.claim: The Dataverse credential table supports the GrantAccess, ModifyAccess and RevokeAccess access actions.
claims.quote: The following operations can be used with the credential entity type. GrantAccess | Not Bound; ModifyAccess | Not Bound; RevokeAccess | Not Bound
claims.fix: Replace the descriptive action list with explicit REST calls POST [organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/GrantAccess, POST [organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/ModifyAccess and POST [organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/RevokeAccess. These are unbound actions, not credential-bound routes. Cite the individual action references and https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/use-web-api-actions.

claims.claim: The Dataverse credential table supports create, read, update and delete operations.
claims.quote: Entity set path: [organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/credentials. Operations supported: POSTGETPATCHDELETE

claims.claim: In the planned Delinea unattended integration, a stored identity retrieves the machine password.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate Delinea Secret Server privileged machine password stored identity unattended automation. Read the roadmap, both cited credential guides and the Power Automate for desktop architecture excerpt; none states the Delinea retrieval identity or its storage.
claims.fix: Replace 'where a stored identity retrieves a privileged machine password with no person present' with 'which does not require human supervision'. Retain the following statement that the Delinea authentication method is not yet published.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The machine credentials retrieved through Delinea are privileged credentials.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate Delinea Secret Server privileged machine password stored identity unattended automation; Power Automate desktop flows unattended credentials stored sign in user account administrator privileges. The roadmap says machine sign-in, not privileged credentials.
claims.fix: Remove 'privileged' before 'machine password' and 'machine credentials'. Alternatively state as analysis: 'If teams use privileged machine accounts, those privileges determine the potential exposure.'

claims.claim: Unattended desktop automation does not require human supervision.
claims.quote: Unattended desktop flows are ideal for automating tasks that don't need human supervision.
claims.fix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/desktop-flows/run-unattended-desktop-flows for the general unattended-run behaviour.

claims.claim: General Power Automate controls also govern desktop flows, although Delinea-specific behaviour is not documented.
claims.quote: Protecting sensitive data is critical when automating processes with Power Automate. This article explains best practices and actionable steps to secure your data: setting up credentials, managing sensitive variables, controlling access to desktop flows and related components
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/guidance/desktop-flow-coding-guidelines/secure-your-data to sources for the general desktop-flow controls, while preserving the explicit caveat that Delinea-specific applicability is not confirmed.
